title: Look up a rule by ID
summary: Follow one rule ID through command dispatch, catalog lookup and a readable explanation.

steps.label: Dispatch
steps.title: Route the rules command
steps.explanation: The top-level entry point sees rules as the first argument and hands the remaining arguments to _main_rules. The normal scan path is bypassed.
steps.insight: A catalog lookup does not read or scan repository instruction files.
steps.transition: The rules parser receives just the command arguments.

steps.label: Parse
steps.title: Read the optional rule ID
steps.explanation: The rules parser accepts an optional rule_id and a --json flag. Supplying an ID selects a single-rule path; omitting it selects the full catalog.
steps.insight: This guide follows one ID. The list-all path uses the same Rule objects.
steps.transition: _main_rules uses the parsed ID for a catalog lookup.

references.quote:
def build_rules_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="agent-config-score rules",
        description="List all stable rule IDs or explain one rule in detail.",
    )
    p.add_argument("rule_id", nargs="?", help="Optional rule ID, for example: curl-pipe-shell")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="Print machine-readable JSON")
    return p

steps.label: Lookup
steps.title: Find the canonical rule
steps.explanation: RULES_BY_CODE maps each unique rule ID to a Rule. get_rule uses a dictionary lookup and returns None if the ID is unknown. The curl-pipe-shell definition supplies severity, category, penalty and description.
steps.insight: The scanner and this explanation command share the same catalog entry.
steps.transition: The caller checks whether a matching Rule exists.

references.quote:
def get_rule(code: str) -> Rule | None:
    return RULES_BY_CODE.get(code)

RULES = (
    Rule("curl-pipe-shell", "error", "danger", 18, "Remote script piped directly to a shell", "Flags persistent instructions that pipe curl output directly into sh or bash."),

steps.label: Check ID
steps.title: Handle an unknown ID explicitly
steps.explanation: When the catalog returns None, the command prints an error to stderr and returns 2. With a known ID, it continues to the selected output format.
steps.insight: An unknown ID does not turn into an empty successful explanation.

steps.label: Explain
steps.title: Print the rule, then finish
steps.explanation: Without --json, the command prints the ID, severity, category, penalty, summary and description. With --json, it serializes the Rule dictionary. Both known-rule paths return 0.
steps.insight: Penalty 18 is catalog metadata here. This command does not calculate a repository score.
